title: The Last Tend Holds

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: A figure kept in a fist costs nothing; a place kept on a shelf costs a loaf a day and nobody counts it.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the clay-bound, Low Kiln

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-thirteen-to-one-hundred-and-fifteen-day-old body carried everywhere; the surgeon's register colours the noticing (a fist shutting on a figure read as a chart closed with a neat line over an unread note, a neighbour reaching past a bare board read as an exact and worthless sorting, the damper's double bite read as the clamp that holds and the clamp that takes, the held breath read as a breath stopped against iron) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, Waiting Room, collector or back-room interior

scenes.title: The Figure That Arrives Nowhere
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 113, Seed 24, Fourthday, morning at the loaf shelf in the Vail kiln-house and at the yard well. The last tend stands in the worked strips east of Low Kiln, the seed up, the hands still counted in glances and handfuls and never in a figure. Sella Vail gives the instruction to the bucket, the broom, the pot and the fire before anybody and never to the basket, says the house, keeps the half-pace from every open slate and moves her lips along the row. A woman with wet sleeves asks what the planting cost now that hands have been in the strips; Sella glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze on the wall shelf, leaves the space at the row's end with no figure and sends her to the pot with ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there, because the house has said it. Berr Clay is not on stage this day; a man brings a number up out of a fist toward the well, looks at it, thinks better of giving it and puts the fist back in his sleeve, so the figure arrives nowhere. The boy, one hundred and thirteen days old and told by nobody, reads the shut fist as a chart closed with a neat line over a note not opened --- exact, complete, worth nothing --- and his hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the worked strip and comes down. Advances T077 and T058/T079 (instruction to the pot, never the basket; the house's arithmetic in loaves and glances; figure withheld at its source), T009/T013/T092 (left things kept), T071/T072 (113). Withheld: no figure, no cause, no joining, no payment, no ending.

scenes.title: Two Absences in One Breath
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry continued, Day 113, midday at the loaf shelf and going of the light under the Vail kiln-house roof. Another neighbour at the shelf reaches past the bare board, calls the old space at the row's end a thing the planting brought in and the empty place at the boy's ear a child's appetite in one breath, and goes off with her pot without seeing that she has laid two rooms under one cause. The boy keeps the shelf's two gaps, the fold's one stiff brown-edged crust and its unnamed empty place, and the neighbour's saying on three places that do not touch; T097 advanced again and not paid, no fourth likeness allowed to make a cause and no third gap. Sella glances at the clay jar and gives nobody a figure and does not touch the widow's mark, because a shelf is not an opening. At the going of the light she sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and leaves the thread at his mouth frozen and unwiped, because nobody has been given an instruction about the thread. He turns out the private file as a man lays instruments on a towel and finds every object where he left it: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, three intervals, the word forty unspoken with the readable double turn and the weight of a thumb apart, four low things in four places with the river's note a fifth, the two tellings of the shut room joined to no kiln, the damper's double bite filed as an object, the loan that can hear uncalled. The carried fire answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and thirteen days. Advances T097 (advanced, not paid), T060/T086, T058/T079, T061/T082, T036/T076, T088, T071/T072 (113). Withheld: no joining, no name, no third gap, no seventh hearing, no ending.

scenes.title: The Stroke That Does Not Check
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 114, Seed 25, Fifthday, before first grey through midday at the Vail wheel-shed and its finger's-width-open back room (not entered), the damper and the Clay Yard. Men unnamed come up the yard before first grey and speak low in the room that stands a finger's width open; Jorra Vail gives the house no name for them and does not say the room was cold. He comes through with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bent little finger, ground small as meal and not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel, and the boy keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate. Jorra speaks to the wheel before anyone --- it does not care whose hands, only if they are steady --- tells a pot You'll do, knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and will not say so before a kiln-master from High Kiln. When Sella has not finished telling him the fire is low his bent finger goes into the cold iron of the damper ahead of her sentence and the household straightens around his silence the way cloth straightens when a weight is lifted. Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed; this time his stroke does not check behind the standing finger but goes on over the flagstones without a pause and without a turn of the head. The first fraction of change is held, not repeated and not explained: the flagstones still keep the place where the stroke stopped the day before, neither man names the other's silence and the loan that can hear is still uncalled. The boy reads the iron once more as the bite that holds a vessel whole and the bite that can take the hand off a man, with no word in Grathic for both mercies, files it as an object joined to no kiln, and sets the unchecking stroke beside the earlier half-beat without laying a cause across them. Ulda is offstage; no foundling turns late at any board. Advances T035/T031, T062, T036/T076 (first fraction held, not repeated, loan uncalled), T058/T079, T061/T082, T071/T072 (114). Withheld: no naming of the room, no birth-slate opened, no repeating of the check, no calling of the loan, no spending of the seventh year.

scenes.title: Warm and Breathing
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry continued, Day 114, midday three doors down in House Silt and going of the light under the Vail roof. Sella sets the basket just inside the finger's-width-open door at the edge of the light and away from every place a slate might lie, opens no slate and turns no errand into a walk to Slate Row. Alda Reed lays her birth-slates writing-down on the bench before she turns to the fold, presses the wool a breath too long, crosses two fingers at the red edge of the birth-flower before she knows it and covers the sign with the date she gave Dessa, says Warm and breathing, that's all I've set down --- exact and not true over a woman more mornings dead than any living person keeps count of --- and goes on with dates after the question has stopped. Her hand goes once into her bodice to the little tin and comes away without opening it; the sixth narrow slate stays face-down toward a floorboard in a house the boy cannot name, six pages in a second hand all unread, no seventh written and T023 not paid again. Above the abandoned board-bed the round pewter tin keeps its pale fold and thumb-bright rub unopened while the grey wool below holds only the hollow where the small pale river stone had lain, and nobody says either is gone. Under the roof at the going of the light the boy turns out the file and finds it unchanged and adds what the day gave without entering any of it: the men unnamed, the grey dust, Jorra's finger in the iron and Tarn's stroke going on without the check, held on one tray and not joined. One crust stays stiff in the fold with its empty place unnamed and no third; the shelf's two gaps stay in the other room; below the sill the dark foot stays dark inside three turns of wool, cold to one woman and weather to the yard, the extremity going before the core read perfectly and buying nothing. Advances T023/T089 (not paid again), T007/T008/T073, T035/T031, T036/T076, T061/T082, T093/T094/T096, T060/T086, T071/T072 (114). Withheld: no name or number from Dessa, no tin opened, no seventh page, no silt-leach, no recognition.

scenes.title: The Figure at the Edge of the Slate
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 115, Seed 26, Sixthday, dawn at the Fishstairs below the north bridge and at the outer boards of the fish-trade shade, then the Cross. Sella sets the basket where no slate lies and gives the instruction to the wool and the running water and never to the basket, standing a half-pace from every open slate. Mira Silt works the eels with pale slime dried on her sleeves and silt dried pale in the hollow of her neck, her head held a little to the right where the top of her left ear had been, her small smile kept like a door on the latch; asked whether the run will be thin she answers her own answer, Thin? Who's to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river, moves eel-bones against her thumb while deciding whether to lie and puts one away. When a buyer names a figure her thumb goes under her apron to the grey cord and a shift of the creel shows the second cord twisted twice beneath it, never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted, the knot for the thin child upriver untouched; her board lies beside Orra Weir's knot-string and does not touch it, Orra offstage and present only as the board. At the Cross a man from Slate Row whose name is on no roll is glimpsed again handing a figure to a slate with his soft hands, holding the slate at the edge where nobody else can see the figure and resting his thumb on the corner afterward without passing it over the number as Berr would. The boy files him apart from the pause in the neat dark hand, the Drawing collector's grey fingertips, the Court-table clerk, the soft-cuffed Fishstairs clerk still set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called, and the watcher; no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand, no loaf passing, no secret changing hands that a slate could read, and no sale. Advances T059/T025/T024, T090/T080, T083, T061/T082, T071/T072 (115). Withheld: no knot counted, no word forty, no sixth sighting, no sale, no watcher on stage.

scenes.title: One Hundred and Fifteen
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry continued, Day 115, going of the light under the Vail kiln-house roof. The boy is one hundred and fifteen days old, three months and twenty-five days, and nobody under the roof knows there is a number to be known; he has stopped expecting to be told, which is not the same as not wanting it. He turns out the private file as a man lays instruments on a towel and finds it unchanged: six hearings of the full note beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, three intervals, the word forty unspoken with the readable double turn and the weight of a thumb apart, four low things in four places with the river's note of water over water a fifth, the two tellings of the shut counting room joined to no kiln and no third, the damper's double bite filed as an object worth nothing, the held breath from Seed 16 still unspent, the unforged collector sentence kept beside it and the loan that can hear uncalled. The told bell stays beside the heard bell; the bell was not heard in this chapter and is not invented. One brown-edged crust lies stiff in the fold with its empty place unnamed and no third; the shelf keeps its two unnamed gaps in a room that does not touch this one; below the sill the dark foot stays uncured, uncaused and unnamed; the clean dark line and the new finer grey lie unswept and are called the thaw; the space under the lowest rack is gone around and entered by nobody; no opening came, so the widow's mark hangs untouched and Sella's private roll stays unshown. The carried fire lies under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, giving back four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and fifteen days. Sella tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says the house will keep it where another woman would say I, stands a moment with the back of the pot in her hand counting something under her breath that no man could take up as a figure, pushes a strand of coal-black hair back with the wrist that carries the little-door burn (the grey streak at her temple pale in the dying light), sets the pot where it could be found in the dark and does not look toward the bed. The door stands a finger's width open; the river's note comes through the gap and the kiln's four, four and a gap through the floor, two sounds in two places that have not met in a hundred and fifteen days. The boards overhead keep four nails, four, and a fifth that is a knot the width of a thumb. Cold arrives cheek, temple, wrist, the wool riding back from the bare joint. His hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water over water and comes down. One hundred and fifteen stands where one hundred and fourteen stood, exact, unspent, spoken by nobody, and on the morrow one hundred and sixteen will stand in the same place. Advances T071/T072 (115, unspent), T061/T082, T060/T086, T036/T076, T088, T009/T013/T092, T093/T094/T096, T058/T079. Withheld: no ending, no payment, no joining, no seventh hearing, no third crust, no calling of the loan.
